central_claim_as_understood: The NR4A3 5' fusion partner is a CANDIDATE - not established - stratification variable in EMC. Prognosis now has a crude two-cohort magnitude (7/15 = 46.7% TAF15 vs 6/58 = 10.3% EWSR1 over 73 patients, post-hoc Fisher p = 0.0034) arriving with its own defeater. Treatment response has a DIRECTION only - 0 of 3-5 TAF15 patients, a zero-event arm that yields no magnitude at any denominator. Prevalence is 28/154 = 18.2% (12.9-25.0).
method: An enumerated single-token mutation sweep over ALL 1,298 numeric tokens in the pinned manuscript (609 caught, 689 survived), cross-checked against a direct span analysis of the two guards' BINDINGS, DECLARED_NOT_ARTIFACT_OWNED and COUNT_WORDS patterns, with every hypothesis re-proved by an isolated mutation run against the full 1,545-test manuscripts suite plus lint_citations and lint_claims. Two private detached worktrees at the pin, both verified clean and removed; the shared tree was never written to.

blockers.where: research/manuscripts/tests/test_fusion_partner_prose_matches_its_artifact.py lines 2214-2218 (the identifier census's stated scope), at the pin
blockers.what: The comment that justifies excluding PMC ids from the identifier census contains three statements that are false at the pin. (1) 'the three the pooling artifact holds a structured field for: pmid, doi, nct ... the artifact has no `pmc` field' - the artifact holds `pmcid` on 11 of its 17 citation records, including stacchiotti2020review -> PMC7563993. (2) 'a PMC id is printed 23 times in this manuscript' - it is printed 12 times in the manuscript and 25 times across the two prose documents the guard actually reads. (3) 'Widening to PMC would mean either inventing a home for it or declaring 23 sites' - the home exists, EVERY PMCID the manuscript prints is already owned by that field (0 declarations), and the only unowned ones are the 3 in the correction register, which are precisely the three papers register row A11 names in order to say they are NOT the review - the same shape as the existing DECLARED_IDENTIFIERS_NOT_POOLED rows.
blockers.why_blocking: The false premise is load-bearing: it is the whole stated reason a surface goes unread, and the census's own header three lines above says 'IT CANNOT SEE ATTACHMENT, AND ATTACHMENT IS THE DEFECT THIS DOCUMENT HAS ALREADY MADE ONCE' - an attribution error that was itself about PMCIDs (register A11). PROVEN, not asserted: swapping the two real, anchored PMCIDs on reference entries [7] Agaram 2014 (PMC4015728) and [11] Brenca 2019 (PMC6766969) leaves the whole manuscripts suite at 1545 passed / 3 skipped - byte-identical to the clean baseline - plus lint_citations exit 0 and lint_claims exit 0. Swapping PMC7563993 for another real review's PMCID at S3.3/S5 - the n=1 attribution the paper's entire metastasis negative rests on - is caught only incidentally, because the word 'review' happens to sit beside it.

blockers.what: 'Its TAF15 share over assigned cases (7 of 26) is the highest of any series here' is FALSE. 7/26 = 26.9%; the artifact holds Agaram 2014 at 7/24 = 29.2% (pooled) and Sjogren 2003 at 3/9 = 33.3% (excluded). It is third, not highest.
blockers.why_blocking: A wrong comparative claim in the artifact the manuscript declares (S7) to be 'the one home of every number in this paper'. It was already false when written - Agaram was 29.2% before Sjogren was added - and adding Sjogren made it false twice over. It is the exact shape the relations guard was built for ('a superlative carries no digit for a numbers guard to read'), and nothing reads it: the generator's _self_check is arithmetic-only and no test evaluates artifact prose. The manuscript's own version of the same comparison (S3.5) is CORRECT, so no manuscript claim is wrong today - the defect is confined to the artifact.
blockers.driver_confirmed: YES -- 7/26 = 26.9% against Agaram 7/24 = 29.2% and Sjogren 3/9 = 33.3%, and the manuscript's own S3.5 prints the per-cohort range as '15.8 - 29.2', which the artifact's superlative contradicts.

p2s.where: systems/graph/routes.json lines 5575 and 5582 and the generated copies - OUTSIDE the named subject set, reported because it is a live wrong statement about S6 of the subject
p2s.what: 'send the three paywalled-table requests named in its section 6' and 'the three tables ... are already written and simply not public'. S6 names TWO unreachable documents (Stacchiotti 2019; Paioli 2021). The 'three' was correct when written 2026-08-07; S6 dropped Huang 2023 from the list on 2026-08-12 and routes.json was never updated. A silent regression across the document/graph boundary, and it is also the route's best_next_action.

The two ratchets are mis-tensioned in opposite directions. only_declared <= 20 sits at exactly 20 with ZERO headroom, so the next figure landing inside a declaration-only span turns the census red and the tempting fix is to raise the ceiling. Meanwhile in_bindings >= 90 sits at 162 - 72 of slack - so the anti-deletion ratchet cannot fire until roughly half the guard's coverage has been removed along with its sentences.
The section resolver checks EXISTENCE, not correctness - a weaker property than the claim. Mutating S2.3 -> S2.4 and S3.3 -> S3.4 both pass, because the target sections exist.

Journal, volume, page and year in every reference entry are unbound although the artifact holds journal/year (and volume/pages for several). Mutating '2014;50:1657-64' or '2019;20:1252-62' passes. CONVERGENT with the citations seat's CITE-B-1, which found a live wrong locator in exactly this unread surface.
